page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapping to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, placing in the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core and top 25% for stress-ng multi-core. Cryptographic and integer operations are accelerated by hardware support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is in the top 25% at 4967.9 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average tier.

Given its balanced resource distribution and strong computational capabilities, the n4d-standard-48 is optimized for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, text and image processing, and database operations. It also shows high efficiency in small-scale LLM inference, reaching top-tier token generation speeds with a 135M model and strong speeds with a 7B model. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of modern AMD EPYC compute resources relative to its memory footprint, though workloads requiring massive local storage or high uncached memory bandwidth may face performance bottlenecks.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-48 is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, utilizing the AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 24 physical cores. It lacks bundled local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core capabilities and strong multi-core execution, particularly in text processing, image processing, and software compilation. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI, which accelerate cryptographic and vector calculations. While cached memory bandwidth is highly competitive, uncached large-block memory operations perform at average levels. This instance is optimized for balanced workloads such as database operations, static web serving, and small-to-medium language model inference, offering a resource-dense configuration for compute-heavy general-purpose applications.
